sentence: Spectrum Considerations

sentence: Equation (2) shows that B and B + B² are similar, so they have the same set (with multiplicity) of eigenvalues.
sentence-category-reason: Announces the focus on spectral properties as the next approach.

sentence: Now, if λ is any eigenvalue of B then λ is also an eigenvalue of A B A⁻¹.

sentence:
On the other hand, if v is an eigenvector of B with eigenvalue λ then (provided v is an eigenvector for B+B²—a point we discuss below) one would have
  (B+B²)v = (λ + λ²)v.
sentence-category-reason: States a property of eigenvalues under similarity; conceptual inference.

sentence: Thus the eigenvalues of B+B² are exactly of the form λ+λ².

sentence:
Since the spectra of B and B+B² must agree it follows (as multisets) that
  {λ : λ is an eigenvalue of B} = {λ + λ² : λ is an eigenvalue of B}.
sentence-category-reason: Concludes the eigenvalues of B+B² are of the form λ+λ².

sentence:
This “spectrum‐matching” condition forces the eigenvalues of B to obey the rule that for every eigenvalue λ there is (possibly the same or another) eigenvalue μ of B with
  μ = λ + λ².

sentence: Let us now analyze this requirement.

In that case the matching condition gives

sentence: But this number is n.
